notes.5: Many correct solutions were seen, showing a good understanding of differentiation and coordinate geometry. Provided a candidate was able to differentiate the given equation correctly, most went on to obtain the gradient of the normal at the given point and hence the equation of the normal. The subsequent calculations to obtain the coordinates of the intercepts with the axes and the resulting mid-point were usually correct with the occasional arithmetic slip. ( )
notes.8: (i) Most candidates made the appropriate use of the remainder theorem and the factor theorem to obtain two equations which could then be solved simultaneously. There were occasional arithmetic slips, but many correct solutions were seen. The few candidates who chose to attempt algebraic long division rarely made progress. Algebraic long division is to be discouraged in questions of this type. (ii) Algebraic long division or factorisation by observation was intended for this part of the question with both methods being used to great effect. Provided candidates had correct values from part (i), a correct response was usually seen. For those who did not have the correct values in part (i), most were usually able to obtain a method mark for a correct approach. (iii) Candidates were not expected to make use of their calculator to solve the quadratic equation obtained from using their quadratic factor from part (ii), hence the use of the word ‘exact’. Too many used their calculator and gave decimal answers. For those that did not obtain the correct quadratic factor in part (ii), some were able to obtain a method mark for a correct approach. Candidates are to be reminded of the importance of checking that their answers are in the required form. ( )(

notes.key_messages: Candidates should ensure that they read each question carefully and check that they have responded to all the demands in full. Special notice should be taken of the requirement for an exact answer, which implies that a calculator should not be used in the final calculations. In spite of instructions not to use a calculator in the question involving surds, some candidates ignored this. As a result, they were unable to gain any marks for this particular question. It was also noted that, in the question requiring the candidate to show a particular trigonometric result, some candidates persistently failed to write the appropriate angle with their trigonometric ratio. In theory, the work they produced was meaningless. Candidates are to be encouraged to set their work out correctly and not to attempt short cuts of this fashion. The meaning of the word ‘Hence’, when it appears in an examination paper of this type, is not understood by some candidates. When the word ‘Hence’ appears at the start of a part question, it is intended that candidates make use of a previous result they have obtained. When the phrase ‘Hence or otherwise’ appears, it is intended that candidates will probably find it easier to do the question using a result obtained in the previous part, but may use another method should they wish. In the question on matrices, they did not have the latter option.
notes.general_comments: All candidates appeared to have enough time to complete the paper and usually enough space for their answers, if they set their work out concisely. Candidates should be encouraged to think about the structure of their response in the limited space that is available and try to set out their response in a neat and orderly fashion. Rather than write in margins or continue into the spaces for the following questions, candidates should either make use of any blank pages in the examination booklet or request an extra sheet or two of paper. A statement to the effect that the question is continued elsewhere will ensure that the work is located easily and given any credit due
